messages.subject: orientdb as a new sql backend??
messages.subject_clean: orientdb as a new sql backend??
messages.body_plain:
Hi, I was reading https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/dplyr/vignettes/new-sql-backend.html and trying to understand whether orientdb could be added as a new sql backend. Orientdb is a mix of a document and graph database, but uses a SQL language for querying. That being said, what starts as SQL later gets extended "to support more complex graphing concepts, such as Trees and Graphs"  http://orientdb.com/docs/2.1/Tutorial-SQL.html

to summarize, my question at this point is simply: how can I evaluate whether an orientdb backend for dbplyr would be possible?

ricardo

Hi Ricardo,

I think the best way to start is to think about how you'd translate
basic dplyr verbs (e.g. filter(), arrange(), mutate()) in to
operations in OrientDB.

Hadley

messages.subject: trouble with mutate, unsupported type for column (NILSXP, classes = NULL)
messages.subject_clean: trouble with mutate, unsupported type for column (NILSXP, classes = NULL)
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I am new to R so I am unsure how to provide all information necessary to help with my problem.
I am accessing a sqlite db from R using RSQLite and also using JSONLite to process JSON.
The SQLite data has columns with large integers (milliseconds since 1970) that it uses as primary keys.
I am trying to access data in my decoded JSON blob in mutate, in order to provide human readable values in the data table.

The order of operations isː

1) connect to sqlite db
2) use dbReadTable to collect JSON data
3) call fromJSON to parse json blob, store into variable
4) call dbGetQuery to obtain results of query. In query, large integers are cast to type 'text' so they are properly processed by SQLite
5) call mutate to map column in data.frame returned in step 4 to a proper "name" stored in the json bob

My error is:

Error: unsupported type for column 'deck' (NILSXP, classes = NULL)
And my command is :

  revlog2 = mutate(rl2, revtime = as.POSIXct(epochsecs, origin="1970-01-01"), date=as.Date(revtime), deck=decks[[did]]$name)

rl2 is the result of head(revlog, 2) in an attempt to limit the processing to a minimal number of rows, and revlog is the result of step 2 above
when rl2 contains head(revlog, 1) it works fine
but both rows in rl2 contain the same value for "did"

I have confirmed that all possible values of "did" in revlog are contained in the json structure "decks"
The data is too large to paste into an email, and I am not sure what information is useful to diagnose

> decks
$`1427388736082`
$`1427388736082`$desc
[1] ""

$`1427388736082`$name
[1] "Lang::french::French 103"

$`1427388736082`$extendRev
[1] 8

I would appreciaate any help that can be provided and am happy to provide any more information provided I have some idea what to supply.
My version of R is 3.2.2 64 bit on windows 8

Kay

messages.body_plain:
I'm trying to figure out how to write flexible code for subsetting a distance matrix for downstream analysis and plotting.

little.dist <-  structure(list(B.R18 = c(NA, 0.276303, 0.125914, 0.129066, 0.838587, 0.834047), C.C11 = c(NA, NA, 0.339285, 0.314995, 0.770283, 0.759652 ), C.C16 = c(NA, NA, NA, 0.126101, 0.821724, 0.81644), C.C19 = c(NA, NA, NA, NA, 0.799399, 0.793513), HC1 = c(NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, 0.336314), HC5 = c(NA_real_, NA_real_, NA_real_, NA_real_, NA_real_, NA_real_)), .Names = c("B.R18", "C.C11", "C.C16", "C.C19", "HC1", "HC5"), row.names = c("B.R18", "C.C11", "C.C16", "C.C19", "HC1", "HC5"), class = "data.frame")

little.group <- structure(list(invsimpson_hci = c(2.796736, 5.018727, 2.845905, 3.165948, 18.308151, 22.14335), Study = structure(c(2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 4L, 4L), .Label = c("10wkHFD", "4wkSM", "BserumPLT", "Plgutmicrobiota" ), class = "factor"), Diet = structure(c(3L, 12L, 12L, 12L, 4L, 4L), .Label = c("Bserum", "CTL", "ESM", "HFC", "HFDC", "HFE", "HFM", "LFC", "LFDC", "LFE", "LFM", "MSM"), class = "factor"), withinstudyordinance = c(3L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 4L, 4L), Crossstudyordinance = c(0L, 5L, 5L, 5L, 5L, 5L)), .Names = c("invsimpson_hci", "Study", "Diet", "withinstudyordinance", "Crossstudyordinance"), class = "data.frame", row.names =  c("B.R18", "C.C11", "C.C16", "C.C19", "HC1", "HC5"))

My previous clunky way to do this was to create a dist and group object for each Study:

wk4.dist <- little.dist[little.group$Study=="4wkSM",little.group$Study=="4wkSM"]
wk4.group <- little.group[little.group$Study=="4wkSM",little.group$Study=="4wkSM"]

then run downstream analyses. This seems like it'd be a good application for dplyr but I can't figure out how to subset the dist while keeping it square for downstream analyses (I'll be using as.dist on the dataframes)

thanks
